topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the topic of complement and frames its complexity within immunology.

topics.label: Core principles, nomenclature, and C3 activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental concepts of the complement cascade, its historical naming rules, and the central role of C3 cleavage.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the mechanisms of the alternative, lectin, and classical pathways that drive C3 deposition to reach the activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the downstream immunological outcomes of complement activation, including opsonization, inflammatory signaling, and membrane attack complex lysis.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory factors and mechanisms that prevent complement from activating on and damaging host cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the distinct clinical presentations and disease phenotypes resulting from deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how pathogens, specifically Staphylococcus aureus, employ evolutionary strategies to evade complement-mediated killing.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer wraps up the session on complement and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
